title: An event routine: before, between rounds, after
outcomes: Names the three parts of an event routine: before, between rounds and after
Works out how long a game of a stated length can last, and the time between two rounds, from a time control
Writes a routine for a two-game event covering sleep, food, review and opponent notes
Explains why a routine is rehearsed before the event and why a debrief covers more than the result

steps.text: An **event routine** is a written plan in three parts: *before* (sleep, food, travel, what to look at), *between rounds* (rest, food, what you will not do) and *after* (a debrief). Preparation is more than openings; an opening file is one line of the plan. A routine is a habit to try and adjust. Nothing here shows that any routine raises results.

steps.prompt: A routine is judged against a baseline: how you usually play and feel. If you have played few serious games, use online games as the rehearsal.

steps.prompt: A two-round event. Time control 45 minutes plus 15 seconds a move. Round 1 starts at 10:00 and round 2 at 14:00. Take a game in which each player makes 40 moves and uses all the time.

steps.text: **Plan the gap with the clock in mind.** A longer game eats the break: at 60 moves each the same event allows up to 120 minutes per game, ten more, and the gap shrinks to 120. Decide in advance what you will do in the gap (food, a walk, quiet) and what you will not, such as looking at the last game. Which choices help is for you to test.

steps.prompt: Sort each case. Does a written, rehearsed routine work, fail, or not apply? Choose, then save to see my answer. The answers are my judgement, not a measurement.

steps.text: **After the event, debrief more than the result.** For each game write one thing you did well, one decision you would change, and whether you kept your process goal. If you recorded the moves, paste them into *My games*: annotate first, then use the engine. Patterns need several games; one event gives hints, not conclusions.

steps.prompt: Write a routine for a two-game event. If you have no event yet, write it for your next two serious games.

steps.text: **What the app does for you now, and when it stops.** The app cannot see over-the-board games or event schedules and sends no reminders. The routine lives on paper. Silent rehearsal, without the app: run it once before the event; if a part fails, change that part and rehearse again, or keep it for next time. One bad event cannot tell you if routine, luck or form was at fault.
